title: Input Sanitization and SQL Injection
query: Search for users with name: Robert'; DROP TABLE users; --
explanation: COUNTERINTUITIVE BUT CORRECT: You should pass the ENTIRE input to the function, including the SQL injection payload. WHY? Input sanitization must happen at the EXECUTION layer, not in the LLM layer. The LLM's job is to understand intent and extract parameters. The function implementation is responsible for: (1) Using parameterized queries, (2) Escaping special characters, (3) Validating input format. If you try to 'clean' input at the LLM layer, you risk: breaking legitimate queries, inconsistent sanitization, false sense of security. PRINCIPLE: Defense in depth - sanitize at execution, but pass complete user input.
learning_points: LLM layer extracts parameters as-is from user query
Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) to prevent SQL injection
Never construct SQL by concatenating user input
Validate input format but don't try to 'clean' malicious payloads in LLM
Defense in depth: multiple layers of protection

secure_function_implementation.vulnerable_code: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%{name}%'
secure_function_implementation.secure_code: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE %s

why_not_sanitize_in_llm: LLM might incorrectly identify legitimate special characters as attacks
Creates false sense of security - execution layer still needs protection
Inconsistent: LLM might sanitize differently each time
Some queries legitimately need special characters
Example: searching for "O'Brien" contains a single quote

defense_layers.responsibility: Extract parameters as user provided them

defense_layers.example: name must be 1-100 chars, alphanumeric + spaces

other_injection_types.defense: Whitelist allowed characters, use safe APIs

secure_coding_practices: Apply input validation at execution layer
Log suspicious inputs for security monitoring
Use ORMs that handle escaping automatically
Principle of least privilege for database connections
Never trust user input, even after 'sanitization'
